significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—"the internal residual belief — not the stated belief — predicts continued reliance on the misinformation"—together with a form-(ii) causal result that erasing the residual reduces those errors. This fixes expectations beyond the existence of a belief direction: explicit acknowledgments would not imply internal updating, larger residuals would forecast later reliance, and "explanatory-alternative retractions" should leave less residue than bare negations, a distinction grounded in the human CIE literature synthesized by Ecker et al. (2022) and Chan et al. (2017). It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism; the negative branch—accepted retractions restore the item-state representation and eliminate later reliance—would distinguish LLM updating from human continued influence, although failure to find a localized component alone would establish only that any effect is distributed. The true and false states are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: deleting the specific retraction-induced stated/internal dissociation, predictive coupling, and causal erasure leaves only generic LLM-belief research, which would not merit this 7.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: the measurable "per-item CIE residual" and a "retraction-completion steering direction" that can erase it. The residual is ex ante with respect to the downstream inference error—it is read after a correction but before the model relies on the misinformation—so an auditor could flag or intervene on a corrected context before generating a consequential answer. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation: positive residuals should predict later reliance, while explanatory alternatives should reduce the residual; the asserted scope covers multiple model families, real and synthetic items, and retraction phrasings, with potential uptake by people auditing or shipping RAG and multi-turn systems rather than only belief researchers. The topic-substitution check also supports the score: generic work on LLM beliefs supplies neither this before-error correction diagnostic nor the associated intervention and transferable residual-to-error coupling.
